facts.claim: Ethernet frames carry no hop count or time to live, so a looping broadcast frame circles until a port refuses it.
Spanning Tree Protocol elects the root bridge with the lowest bridge ID (priority first, then lowest MAC address) and blocks redundant paths to prevent loops.
Classic 802.1D port states are blocking, listening, learning and forwarding; only forwarding passes user traffic, and learning builds the MAC table without forwarding.
Classic 802.1D defaults are a 2 second hello, 15 second forward delay and 20 second max age, so a direct failure recovers in about 30 seconds and an indirect failure in about 50.

simplifications: Harbor Street is an invented example LAN. Numbers marked assumed are teaching values.
The simulator floods each broadcast out every forwarding port and ignores VLANs, queuing and switch CPU limits; link load is an arbitrary toy scale.
Time is slowed so the 30 second STP walk takes about 12 real seconds.
The simulator shows classic STP. Rapid STP converges faster and uses discarding, learning and forwarding states.
BPDU protection and edge-port settings in ADR-003 go beyond the site's current notes.
